reset.allDesc: Deletes all app data: settings, reading history, scroll positions, open tabs, and the library, catalog and file search indexes. This cannot be undone.

terms.p1: Kitvei Hakodesh is software for studying holy books, part of the "Klei Kodesh" project: a non-profit volunteer initiative that makes Word and the computer accessible to learners and eases their work. The software is free to use.
terms.p3: The books shown are not part of the software. They are read from the book library of Otzaria (or Zayit) installed on the computer, and come from public collections such as Otzaria, Sefaria and others.
terms.p4: All rights in each text belong to their lawful owners. Some books are in the public domain, and some were uploaded with the rights holders' permission or under specific license terms. The texts may not be used commercially, and copyrighted material may not be copied, distributed or published except under the terms set by the rights holders.
terms.p5: If you hold rights in a book and believe it appears unlawfully, please contact the collection it came from, or us, and it will be handled promptly.
terms.p7: The software is provided AS IS, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. The developers are not liable for any damage, direct or indirect, resulting from using the software or being unable to use it.
terms.p9: The texts were typed and processed by people and by computer, and may contain errors and omissions. Checking accuracy is the user's responsibility. Do not rely on the software for practical halachic rulings; ask a qualified rabbi.
terms.p11: We welcome reports of errors in the text or the software. You can report through the error reporting option in the app, helping fix the library for all learners.
terms.p13: The Klei Kodesh project develops a free toolkit for Torah editors and all learners: a library of holy books with search, Torah libraries and websites, Torah document design, vowelization and advanced search. More information and updates on the project site: kleikodesh.github.io
terms.p14: May we merit to make Torah great and glorious.
